extracted.intended_audience: Users/authors of Isabelle/Isar theories and documents (Isabelle/HOL developers, proof authors preparing LaTeX/PIDE documents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal rules for producing typeset documents and embedding formal entities from Isabelle/Isar theory sources (markup commands, antiquotations, document markers, tags, railroad diagrams, and related options). Intended for authors who prepare printable/hyperlinked PDF output or PIDE views from Isabelle theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markup commands (chapter/section/.../text/txt/text_raw)
rubrics_metrics.description: chapter : any → any, section : any → any, subsection : any → any, subsubsection : any → any, paragraph : any → any, subparagraph : any → any, text : any → any, txt : any → any, text_raw : any → any. Markup commands provide a structured way to insert text into the document generated from a theory. Each markup command takes a single text argument, which is passed as argument to a corresponding LaTeX macro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default LaTeX macros are provided by ~~ /lib/texinputs/isabelle.sty and can be redefined. Markup commands mark section headings and work in any context (even before the initial theory command). text and txt specify paragraphs (mapped to an isamarkuptext environment); text_raw injects arbitrary LaTeX without surrounding markup environment. Formal comments (§3.3.5) are similar in purpose but have a different syntactic/status role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document antiquotations — general form and short form
rubrics_metrics.description: Antiquotations are in general written as @{name [options] arguments}. The short form \<^name>‹argument_content› (without surrounding @{...}) works for a single argument that is a cartouche; a bare control symbol \<^name> without a subsequent cartouche is equivalent to @{name}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cartouche without special decoration is equivalent to @{cartouche ‹...›}; cartouche is an alias for text in the context. Antiquotations are interpreted in the present theory or proof context and may therefore refer to formal entities. The syntax of antiquotations may not include source comments (* ... *) nor verbatim text {* ... *}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using antiquotations to embed formal entities and get consistency-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: All text passed to markup commands may refer to formal entities via document antiquotations: these are interpreted in the present theory or proof context and ensure some degree of consistency between formal text and informal explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antiquotations spare tedious typing of logical entities and, because they are checked in the current context, help ensure the informal explanation stays consistent with the formal development. Example: embedding @{term [show_types] "f x = a + x"} within a text block prints the term annotated with its type in the final LaTeX document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antiquotation kinds and semantics (common variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of named antiquotations exist to print or check specific formal objects: @{text s} (uninterpreted source text), @{theory_text s} (uninterpreted theory source), @{theory A} (session-qualified theory name), @{thm a1...an} (print theorems), @{prop φ}, @{lemma φ by m}, @{term t}, @{value t}, @{term_type t}, @{typeof t}, @{const c}, @{abbrev c x1...xn}, @{typ τ}, @{type κ}, @{class c}, @{locale c}, @{bundle c}, @{command name}, @{method name}, @{attribute name}, @{goals}, @{subgoals}, @{prf a1...an}, @{full_prf a1...an}, @{ML_text s}, @{ML ...} and ML variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate antiquotation for each formal object; full fact expressions are allowed in @{thm}. @{prf} / @{full_prf} print compact or full proof terms (require proof terms to be enabled). @{ML...} variants check and print ML fragments and have def/ref variants to affect the document index: 'def' makes a bold index entry, 'ref' a regular entry. @{goals} prints the dynamic goal state and is mainly for tactic-emulation scripts; the manual notes that presentation of goal states does not conform to human-readable proof documents and recommends spelling out reasoning via proper Isar proof commands when explaining proofs in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Styled antiquotations (lhs, rhs, concl, prem n)
rubrics_metrics.description: The antiquotations thm, prop and term accept an extra style specification (a name and optional arguments) to modify the printed result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard styles include: lhs (extract first argument of application forms with ≥2 args), rhs (extract second), concl (extract conclusion C from a Horn-clause form A1 =⇒ ... =⇒ C), prem n (extract premise number n). Multiple styles can be sequenced with commas.

rubrics_metrics.name: General options tuning antiquotation printed output
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of options control how antiquotations print their result: show_types, show_sorts, show_structs, show_abbrevs, names_long, names_short, names_unique, eta_contract, display, break, cartouche, quotes, mode, margin, indent, goals_limit, source, source_cartouche.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meanings: show_types/show_sorts toggle printing explicit type/sort constraints; names_long/short/unique control qualification of names; eta_contract controls η-contraction; display forces multi-line display material; break controls line breaks; cartouche/quotes control delimiters; mode adds a print mode (default 'latex'); margin/indent affect pretty-printing; goals_limit caps number of subgoals shown; source=true prints original source text rather than internal representation (still checks well-formedness); source_cartouche preserves cartouche delimiters. For Boolean flags, 'name = true' may be abbreviated as 'name'. All flags are disabled by default unless set in the ROOT file for the logic session. Regular term/typ antiquotations with source=false perform a full round-trip to internal representation and back, so printed output may change as the theory evolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: print_antiquotations
rubrics_metrics.description: print_antiquotations∗ : context → prints all document antiquotations defined in the current context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The '!' option indicates extra verbosity. Useful to inspect which antiquotations are available in a context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markdown-like text structure (Isabelle quasi-Markdown rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text, txt, text_raw markup arguments use a minimal Markdown-like structure: paragraphs and nested lists are formed using special Isabelle symbols and indentation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List markers: itemize: \<^item>, enumerate: \<^enum>, description: \<^descr>. Adjacent items with same indentation and marker group into one list. Singleton blank lines separate paragraphs; multiple blank lines escape current list hierarchy. Differences from common Markdown: list indentation must match exactly; indentation is unlimited; list items always consist of paragraphs (no 'tight' lists); section headings are expressed via Isar markup commands (§4.1). URLs, font styles, and other special content are expressed via antiquotations, usually nested via text cartouches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document markers and command tags (syntax, effects, and defaults)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document markers are formal comments of the form \<^marker>‹marker_body› and may occur anywhere within outer syntax of a command; command tags may only occur after a command keyword and are treated as special markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markers are stripped from the document output but surrounding whitespace is preserved. Markers operate within the semantic presentation context and may modify it (e.g., by adding tags). Predefined markers include title, creator, contributor, date, license, description (Dublin Core vocabulary) — these produce PIDE document markup but not immediate typesetting; 'description' words are subject to spell-checking. (cid:48)‹tag name› updates the list of command tags (later declarations take precedence); optional scope (proof/command) determines how far tagging applies. Old-style %name is treated like (cid:48)‹tag (proof) name›. Default tags include: document (document markup commands), theory (theory begin/end), proof (all proof commands), ML (commands involving ML code). Tags are turned into LaTeX environments; tag markers can be interpreted by document tools to keep, drop, or fold corresponding parts. Example: 'by auto (cid:48)‹tag invisible›' marks that proof piece as invisible by default; 'tag visible' forces it shown. Explicit tag specifications within a proof apply to subsequent commands at the same nesting level. Logic sessions may define document versions where tags are given specific interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rail antiquotation for syntax diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: rail : antiquotation allows inclusion of syntax (railroad) diagrams into Isabelle documents. The rail specification is quoted as an Isabelle string or text cartouche and has its own grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LaTeX requires ~~ /lib/texinputs/railsetup.sty (use via \usepackage{railsetup} in root.tex). The rail language supports rule definitions (identifier ':' body ';'), concatenation, alternation ('|'), optional ('?'), repetition ('*' and '+'), repetition with separator, grouping via parentheses, terminals via single-quoted strings or antiquotations, and newlines inside concatenations. The manual provides representative examples and semantics; use rail when needing graphical syntax diagrams in the generated document.

rubrics_metrics.name: thm_deps command (immediate theorem dependencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: thm_deps thms prints immediate theorem dependencies — the union of all theorems that are used directly to prove the argument facts, without going deeper into the dependency graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to inspect which theorems are directly used by given theorems/facts; does not traverse deeper into dependency graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: unused_thms command (detect unused theorems across theory ranges)
rubrics_metrics.description: unused_thms A1 ... Am − B1 ... Bn displays all theorems that are proved in theories B1 ... Bn or their parents but not in A1 ... Am or their parents and that are never used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n is 0, the end of the range defaults to the current theory. If no range is specified, only the unused theorems in the current theory are displayed. Useful for cleaning up proved but never-used results across theory hierarchies.
